title: Issue of shares & debentures
examples: What is the difference between shares and debentures?
When do we record the premium on shares?

explain.say: Today we learn about issuing shares and debentures. This involves recording specific accounting entries.

items: Shares represent ownership in a company.
Debentures are a form of loan to the company.
Premium and forfeiture are key concepts.

explain.say: First we look at the share premium. This is extra money received above the face value.
If shares are issued at a premium, the premium amount is credited to the Securities Premium Account.

draw.text: Premium credited to Securities Premium A/c

explain.say: Next we study forfeiture of shares. This happens when a shareholder fails to pay calls or dues.
When shares are forfeited, the company cancels the shares and records the amount paid as 'Share Forfeiture Account'.

draw.text: Forfeiture: Amount paid kept by company

explain.say: In a real-life scenario, if a shareholder buys shares and later defaults, the company may forfeit them. They keep the money already paid.

faq.q: What is the difference between premium and discount on shares?
faq.a: A premium is money received above the face value. A discount is money received below the face value, which is usually not allowed.
asks: Can shares be issued at a discount?
What is the rule for share premium?

faq.q: Why does a company forfeit shares?
faq.a: A company forfeits shares when the shareholder fails to pay the money that was called up on those shares.
asks: What is the consequence of non-payment?
When can shares be cancelled by the company?

faq.q: Where is the premium amount recorded in the books?
faq.a: The premium amount received is credited to the Securities Premium Account, not to the Share Capital Account.
asks: Which account records the extra money?
How is premium treated in accounting?

faq.a: Yes, the company can reissue these shares later, usually at a discount or full value, after following proper accounting steps.
asks: What happens to forfeited shares later?
Is there a process to sell forfeited shares?

faq.q: Is there a limit to the premium amount?
faq.a: The premium must be for legitimate reasons, such as the shares being issued at a premium price.
asks: Are there rules for premium amount?
What justifies issuing shares with premium?

facts: Shares are units of ownership in a company.
A share premium is the excess amount received over the face value.
Forfeiture occurs when a shareholder fails to pay calls.
The amount forfeited is credited to the Share Forfeiture Account.

quiz.say: A company issues shares with a face value of ten rupees and a premium of five rupees. The total amount received per share is:
quiz.why: The total received is the face value plus the premium amount.

wrong.1: This only considers the face value and ignores the premium.
wrong.2: This only considers the premium and ignores the face value.
wrong.3: This suggests no money was received, which is incorrect.

quiz.say: If shares are forfeited, the amount paid by the shareholder is recorded in which account?
quiz.why: This specific account tracks the money already paid by the defaulting shareholder.

wrong.0: This account only records the premium amount received, not the total paid.
wrong.1: While cash is involved, the specific loss/gain is recorded in the Forfeiture Account.
wrong.3: This account records the total nominal value, not the amount forfeited.

quiz.say: A shareholder fails to pay the final call on shares. Which action is most appropriate for the company?

options.show: Write off the entire share amount
options.say: Write off the entire share amount

options.show: Ask the shareholder for a loan
options.say: Ask the shareholder for a loan

quiz.why: Forfeiture is the formal accounting step taken when a shareholder defaults on payments.

wrong.0: Writing off is too drastic; the company retains the paid amount.
wrong.1: This is a business decision, not the formal accounting treatment for default.
wrong.3: While warnings are sent, this is not the final accounting action for non-payment.
